body:
## Category

- [x] CI/CD Workflow (GitHub Actions)
- [x] Test Infrastructure (fixtures, runners, parallelization)

## Description

The Mutation Tests workflow currently runs each mutant against the full ~23,000-test suite because Stryker.NET cannot use `perTest` coverage analysis with xUnit v3 (upstream bug tracked in #1026). This makes kill results semi-stochastic and adding targeted tests yields no measurable improvement — see the empirical evidence in the closing comment of #962.

We can bypass the upstream bug by supplying Stryker with a **manual test-to-source mapping** based on Encina's namespace conventions. Test projects mirror source structure: `src/Encina/Sharding/Migrations/Strategies/*.cs` is tested exclusively by `tests/Encina.UnitTests/Core/Sharding/Migrations/Strategies/*Tests.cs`. So when Stryker is asked to mutate a given folder, we can narrow the `test-case-filter` to only the tests whose namespace mirrors that folder. Each mutant then runs the ~20-50 relevant tests instead of 23,000.

## Component Affected

- **File(s)**:
  - `.github/workflows/mutation-tests.yml` — the `Select mutation scope` step needs to also emit a `TEST_FILTER` output
  - `.github/scripts/run-stryker.cs` — forward the `--test-case-filter` argument when provided
- **Environment**: GitHub Actions `ubuntu-latest`, Stryker.NET 4.14.0, xUnit v3

## Current Behavior

- `custom_scope` input (added in #962) narrows the `--mutate` glob to one folder
- `test-case-filter` in `stryker-config.json` is fixed to the three declared test projects' namespaces (`FullyQualifiedName~Encina.UnitTests|...~Encina.PropertyTests|...~Encina.ContractTests`) — every run ignores that folder's actual scope
- With `coverage-analysis: "off"`, Stryker runs every test against every mutant, which both slows the run (~3 min/mutant × ~60 mutants ≈ 3 h) and makes kills non-deterministic
- Run [24584286635](https://github.com/dlrivada/Encina/actions/runs/24584286635): 1 killed / 58 survived despite 26 mutation-targeted tests being in place

## Expected Behavior

- The `Select mutation scope` step also emits a `TEST_FILTER` output derived from the mutation scope:
  - `**/Sharding/Migrations/Strategies/*.cs` → `FullyQualifiedName~Sharding.Migrations.Strategies`
  - `**/Pipeline/Behaviors/*.cs` → `FullyQualifiedName~Pipeline.Behaviors`
  - ... and so on for each of the 17 rotation entries
- The `Run mutation tests` step passes `--test-case-filter "$TEST_FILTER"` to Stryker, overriding the config value
- Each mutant runs only tests from the matching namespace → ~20-50 per mutant instead of 23,000
- Per-mutant time drops from ~3 min to ~5-10 s
- A folder run completes in ~5-10 min instead of ~3 h
- Kills become deterministic because only tests that actually touch the mutated code path execute

## Impact

- **Developer Experience**: contributors adding mutation-targeted tests see immediate kill-count improvements
- **CI/CD Time**: per-folder run drops from ~3 h to ~5-10 min — ~20× reduction in runner time
- **Reliability**: kill count becomes a stable signal of test quality (no more "3 → 1" regressions from upstream version changes)
- **Unlocks #1027** (matrix-parallel full-project coverage)

## Proposed Solution

### Phase 1: Folder-to-filter map in the workflow

- [ ] Extend the `FOLDERS` array in `.github/workflows/mutation-tests.yml` into a parallel structure that pairs each scope glob with its test filter. Options: two arrays (`FOLDERS` + `FILTERS`) indexed together, or a single associative array.
- [ ] Derive the filter from the scope glob automatically where possible — `**/Sharding/Migrations/Strategies/*.cs` ↔ `Sharding.Migrations.Strategies` is a clean mapping. Edge cases (`**/Core/*.cs` is ambiguous) can be hand-mapped.
- [ ] Emit the filter as a step output alongside the scope.

### Phase 2: Forward filter to Stryker

- [ ] Modify the `Run mutation tests` step to pass `--test-case-filter "$FILTER"` to `run-stryker.cs` when the filter is non-empty.
- [ ] `run-stryker.cs` already forwards unknown args to Stryker; verify no change needed there.

### Phase 3: Validate against the Strategies folder

- [ ] Trigger the workflow with `custom_scope='**/Sharding/Migrations/Strategies/*.cs'`. Expected: kill count jumps from 1 → somewhere in the 20-40 range (of 59 mutants), matching what the 26 targeted tests were designed to catch. Run should complete in ~5-10 min instead of ~3 h.

### Phase 4: Document

- [ ] Update `docs/testing/mutation-measurement-methodology.md`: new section "Per-folder test filter" explaining the manual mapping and its relationship to the upstream perTest bug.
- [ ] Update `CLAUDE.md` "Mutation Testing System" section.

## Risks

- **False negatives**: a contract test in a different namespace that would legitimately kill a mutant in the target folder won't run. For the current 17 rotation folders, source-to-test mapping is tight (dedicated `*Tests.cs` per source file), so the risk is small. If encountered, the fix is to broaden the filter for that specific folder.
- **Namespace drift**: if test namespaces get renamed without updating the mapping, kills silently disappear. Mitigation: the methodology doc documents the mapping convention; reviewers should catch mismatches.

## Related Issues

- #957 — Mutation workflow stabilization (closed)
- #962 — Scope widening + cited-by (closed)
- #1026 — Blocked-upstream: Stryker.NET xUnit v3 perTest bug (this issue is the workaround)
- Unlocks #1027 — Matrix-parallel full-project mutation coverage

## Repro (baseline, before fix)

```bash
gh workflow run "Mutation Tests" --ref main \
  -f custom_scope='**/Sharding/Migrations/Strategies/*.cs'
# Wait ~3h. Observe: 1 killed / 58 survived.
```

## Resumen de la implementación

### Cambios

- **`.github/workflows/mutation-tests.yml`**: Añadido un array `FILTERS` paralelo a `FOLDERS` (17 entradas) que mapea cada carpeta de rotación a una subcadena de namespace de test. El paso `Select mutation scope` emite el filtro como output; el paso `Run mutation tests` parchea `test-case-filter` en `.github/stryker-config.json` con `jq` antes de invocar Stryker. El índice de rotación se deriva de `${#FOLDERS[@]}` y se verifica que `FOLDERS` y `FILTERS` tengan la misma longitud (fail-fast).
- **`docs/testing/mutation-measurement-methodology.md`**: Nueva sección "Per-folder test filter" documentando el mapeo, los casos borde (namespaces raíz, globs no recursivos, tests en ubicaciones inesperadas, `**/Results/*.cs` sin namespace espejo) y el riesgo de deriva de namespaces.
- **`CLAUDE.md`**: Bullet añadido en la sección "Mutation Testing System" recordando mantener `FOLDERS` y `FILTERS` sincronizados.

### Pivote durante revisión

La propuesta inicial usaba `--test-case-filter` como flag de CLI. CodeRabbit detectó que **Stryker.NET 4.14 no expone ese flag por línea de comandos** (solo por archivo de config, ver [stryker-net#3091](https://github.com/stryker-mutator/stryker-net/issues/3091)), lo cual verifiqué localmente con `dotnet stryker --help`. La versión final parchea `stryker-config.json` en sitio con `jq` — los runners de CI son efímeros, así que la edición no se filtra al estado trackeado.

### Otros findings resueltos en la revisión

- **`**/Results/*.cs`**: El filtro propuesto (`Encina.UnitTests.Results|Encina.PropertyTests.Results`) habría seleccionado cero tests porque los tests de los archivos en `src/Encina/Results/` (EitherHelpers, EncinaErrors, NullFunctionalFailureDetector) no viven en ningún namespace `Results`. La entrada se puso vacía para que caiga al filtro por defecto de `stryker-config.json`.
- **Módulo de rotación hardcoded**: `% 17` sustituido por `% ${#FOLDERS[@]}` con assertion de longitud.

### Qué desbloquea esto

- Tiempo por mutante: ~3 min → ~5-10 s (cada mutante ejecuta ~20-500 tests espejo en lugar de ~23k).
- Tiempo por carpeta de rotación: ~3 h → ~5-10 min.
- Conteo de kills determinista: los tests targeted añadidos en #962 (las 26 pruebas de migration strategies) deberían ahora reflejarse en el delta de kills de la próxima rotación.

### Plan de verificación

Lanzar el workflow con `custom_scope='**/Sharding/Migrations/Strategies/*.cs'` y comprobar:

- Runtime de ~5-10 min (vs ~3 h).
- Kills subiendo de 1 → rango 20-40 sobre los 59 mutantes.

Desbloquea #1027 (cobertura matriz-paralela full-project) y relacionado con #1026 (bug upstream bloqueado).
